[*] [b]Rising Recovery[/b]: Press A to quickly recover after getting knocked down. Pressing B will execute a Dodge Roll recovery instead.
[*] [b]Block Breaker[/b]: Hold Y to perform a Block Breaker attack.
[*] [b]Launcher[/b]: Hold X to perform a Launcher attack. This can also be executed while Airborne.
[*] [b]Rising Strike[/b]: While laying on the ground, press any attack button (X or Y) to perform a recovery attack.
[/list]
[h2]Advanced Combat[/h2]
These are Skills that amplify various parts of your Class. It could be related to specific combos, could add additional moves to the kit that are specific to the class (new move, variation of a move, etc). This is where a lot of build crafting comes from.
[list]
[*] [b]Double Jump[/b]: Press A while Airborne to Double Jump.
[*] [b]Explosive Frenzy[/b]: Gain Venom Strikes (5s) after every 30 attacks (count resets when taking damage from an enemy attack). Venom Strikes: Inflict Poison (3s) per hit Poison: deals high damage once per second
[*] [b]Critical Fever[/b]: Light Evade Attack Combo Finisher is guaranteed to critically hit.
[*] [b]Vaulting Smash[/b]: Upgrades the Heavy Evade Attack (B,Y) to Ground Bounce any enemies hit.
[*] [b]Gravity Reset[/b]: After using Light Attacks while Airborne, executing a Double Jump resets the combo counter, allowing for an additional Light Attacks.
[*] [b]Rapid Focus[/b]: Automatically generate Focus while Haste is active.
[*] [b]Elusive Recovery[/b]: When using a Mender's Flask, gain Stealth and Haste (6s). Stealth: Undetectable by enemies until dealing or taking damage Haste: Move speed +15%
[*] [b]Death's Veil[/b]: Gain Stealth (6s) when defeating an enemy with a Focus Skill. Cooldown: 5s Stealth: Undetectable by enemies until dealing or taking damage
[*] [b]Viper's Kiss[/b]: Inflict 2 stacks of Poison (5s) and Weakness (5s) on the final hit of the Advanced Heavy Combo (XYYY). Poison: deals high damage once per second Weakness: -25% DMG
[*] [b]Toxic Eruption[/b]: Heavy Combo Finisher (YYYY) consumes all Poison stacks on the enemy, triggering an explosion. Each stack of Poison increases the explosion damage by 5%.
[*] [b]Serpent's Fang[/b]: Inflict 2 stacks of Poison (5s) on the final hit of the Advanced Light Combo (YXXX). Poison: deals high damage once per second
[*] [b]Quicksteps[/b]: Gain Haste (5s) when using a Focus Skill. Haste: Move speed +15%
[*] [b]Veiled Blast[/b]: Upon entering Stealth, drop a bomb that detonates after 3 seconds. Cooldown: 10s
[*] [b]Divekick[/b]: Press Y after a Double Jump to perform a Divekick attack. By pressing Y at the apex of the Jump, the attack will be enhanced and travel much faster, Block Breaking any enemies hit and inflicting Stun (1s).
[*] [b]Slide Kick[/b]: Press X during a Light Evade Attack to perform a Slide Kick attack.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/83706df7d3d9860c3fbfd3e3e5879daf4a774635.png[/img]

[h3]Light Focus
[/h3][list]
[*] [b]Deathrattle[/b]: Press LT+X to swiftly dash forward, creating a shockwave that damages and Launches enemies. Break Bar DMG: Low
[*] [b]Smoke Veil[/b]: Press LT+X to perform an area attack, and gain Stealth (6s). The Ace is undetectable, gains +50% Crit DMG, and is guaranteed to critically hit while in Stealth. This effect ends if the Ace deals or takes damage. Break Bar DMG: High
[*] [b]Sunrise Shrapnel[/b]: Press LT+X to throw 3 bombs on the ground. After 3 seconds, the bombs detonate, dealing area damage and Launching nearby enemies. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: Medium
[/list][h3]Heavy Focus[/h3]
[list][*] [b]Silver Strikes[/b]: Press LT+Y to execute a 9-hit combo that causes a knockback on the final hit. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High
[*] [b]Lightning Step[/b]: Press LT+Y to unleash a multi-dash attack, Launching enemies and performing a 9-hit airborne combo. The final hit slams enemies into the ground for additional damage. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High
[*] [b]Shooting Stars[/b]: Press LT+Y to throw 2 kunai in front and leap backward, throwing 3 more kunai that deal damage and inflict Poison (3s) per hit on all enemies in the affected area. Break Bar DMG: High
[/list]

- Elusive Recovery: When using a Mender's Flask, gain Stealth and Haste (6s). Stealth: Undetectable by enemies until dealing or taking damage Haste: Move speed +15%
- Death's Veil: Gain Stealth (6s) when defeating an enemy with a Focus Skill. Cooldown: 5s Stealth: Undetectable by enemies until dealing or taking damage
- Viper's Kiss: Inflict 2 stacks of Poison (5s) and Weakness (5s) on the final hit of the Advanced Heavy Combo (XYYY). Poison: deals high damage once per second Weakness: -25% DMG
- Toxic Eruption: Heavy Combo Finisher (YYYY) consumes all Poison stacks on the enemy, triggering an explosion. Each stack of Poison increases the explosion damage by 5%.
- Serpent's Fang: Inflict 2 stacks of Poison (5s) on the final hit of the Advanced Light Combo (YXXX). Poison: deals high damage once per second
- Quicksteps: Gain Haste (5s) when using a Focus Skill. Haste: Move speed +15%
- Veiled Blast: Upon entering Stealth, drop a bomb that detonates after 3 seconds. Cooldown: 10s

- Divekick: Press Y after a Double Jump to perform a Divekick attack. By pressing Y at the apex of the Jump, the attack will be enhanced and travel much faster, Block Breaking any enemies hit and inflicting Stun (1s).
- Slide Kick: Press X during a Light Evade Attack to perform a Slide Kick attack.
- Deathrattle: Press LT+X to swiftly dash forward, creating a shockwave that damages and Launches enemies. Break Bar DMG: Low

- Smoke Veil: Press LT+X to perform an area attack, and gain Stealth (6s). The Ace is undetectable, gains +50% Crit DMG, and is guaranteed to critically hit while in Stealth. This effect ends if the Ace deals or takes damage. Break Bar DMG: High

- Sunrise Shrapnel: Press LT+X to throw 3 bombs on the ground. After 3 seconds, the bombs detonate, dealing area damage and Launching nearby enemies. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: Medium
- Silver Strikes: Press LT+Y to execute a 9-hit combo that causes a knockback on the final hit. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High

- Lightning Step: Press LT+Y to unleash a multi-dash attack, Launching enemies and performing a 9-hit airborne combo. The final hit slams enemies into the ground for additional damage. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High

- Shooting Stars: Press LT+Y to throw 2 kunai in front and leap backward, throwing 3 more kunai that deal damage and inflict Poison (3s) per hit on all enemies in the affected area. Break Bar DMG: High

notes.title: Class Spotlight: Sentinel
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/b9e7641e08a995ae509b354a3e0b408aebe4d44c.png[/img]
[h2]Overview
[/h2]The Sentinel is Towerborne’s sturdy, Sword and Shield swinging all-rounder—combining disciplined defense, precise offense, and seamless combo transitions to transform incoming attacks into decisive counters. Master precise Blocks & Parries to charge Valor Mode—or nail a perfect parry to stun foes and turn defense into instant offense. Seamless ground-and-air combos, reliable damage, and effortless crowd control make the Sentinel ideal for newcomers who want staying power and veterans chasing frame-perfect counters.
[previewyoutube=OGXyN9Hdgx0;full][/previewyoutube]
[h2]Weapon: Sword and Shield[/h2]
Sword and Shield is your trusty go-to. Newcomer-friendly but deep enough to keep battle-hardened Aces grinning, it's uniquely built around solid defense, reliable damage, and smooth combos. Blocking reduces incoming damage, and if you're feeling fancy, masterfully timed parries turn enemy attacks into golden opportunities for brutal counters.
[list]
[*] Fast, fluid combat—perfect for rookies and veterans alike.
[*] Ground and aerial combos that just feel right.
[*] Damage that's as dependable as your best adventuring buddy.
[*] Defensive maneuvers for those who prefer brains and brawn.
[/list][h2]Weapon Mechanic
[/h2]
These are Skills that modify the weapon mechanic (the RB button). Could be expansions to the mechanic, additional options, or even a full on change that makes it feel like something else entirely. 
[list]
[*] Guard: Hold RB to Block. Damage taken while Blocking is reduced by 50%.
[*] Guard II: Damage taken while Blocking is reduced by an additional 10%.
[*] Perilous Guard: When at Critical HP (25% or lower), damage taken while Blocking is reduced by an additional 15%.
[*] Detonating Parry: When at Critical HP (25% or lower), successfully Parrying an attack will trigger an explosion that knocks back nearby enemies.
[*] Mighty Guard: Gain Might (6s) after Blocking 5 attacks. Cooldown: 12s Might: +25% DMG
[*] Parry: Parry an incoming attack by pressing RB right before getting hit.
[*] Mighty Parry: Gain Might (3s) after successfully Parrying an attack. Might: +25% DMG
[*] Debilitating Parry: Inflict Bleed (4s) after successfully Parrying an attack. Bleed: deals medium damage twice per second
[*] Shield Strike: Double tap RB to perform a Shield Strike. This attack Block Breaks.
[*] Shield Surf: While Valor is active, press A while Airborne to perform a Shield Surf attack. 30% chance to inflict Bleed (4s) per hit. Bleed: deals medium damage twice per second
[*] Riposte: Execute a swift counter-attack by pressing any attack button right after successfully Parrying an attack. Inflicts Bleed (4s). Bleed: deals medium damage twice per second
[*] Shield Toss: While Valor is active, press LT+RB to throw the shield. This attack pulls enemies toward the Ace.
[*] Valor: Activate Valor (15s) by pressing LT+RB when the Weapon Meter is full. While Valor is active, holding RB to Block will automatically Parry attacks. Additionally, any incoming damage is reduced by 50%, even when not blocking. Inflict Stun (2s) when successfully executing a Parry by pressing RB right before getting hit.
[*] Blade of Valor: Replaces the 50% incoming damage reduction bonus from Valor with a 20% increase in outgoing damage. Inflict Stun (2s) when successfully executing a Parry by pressing RB right before getting hit.
[*] Unyielding Valor: Increases the duration of Valor by 5 seconds. While Valor is active, successfully executing a Parry by pressing RB right before getting hit extends the duration of Valor by 3 seconds.
[/list] [h2]Standard Moveset
[/h2]These are Skills that modify your most basic combat skills. Need to do a launcher? Cool! Want to dodge in the air? Recovery quickly when knocked down? This is where you do it. All classes have the same Standard Moveset Skills.
[list]
[*] Airborne Shift: Press B while Airborne to Evade.
[*] Heavy Evade Attack: Press Y after Evading to perform a Heavy Evade Attack (B,Y). Evade canceling an attack followed by a Heavy Attack will perform a unique Combo Finisher.
[*] Light Evade Attack: Press X after Evading to perform a Light Evade Attack (B,X). Evade canceling an attack followed by a Light Attack will perform a unique Combo Finisher.
[*] Airborne Rebound: Press A to recover after getting hit while Airborne.
[*] Rising Recovery: Press A to quickly recover after getting knocked down. Pressing B will execute a Dodge Roll recovery instead.
[*] Block Breaker: Hold Y to perform a Block Breaker attack.
[*] Launcher: Hold X to perform a Launcher attack.
[*] Rising Strike: While laying on the ground, press any attack button (X or Y) to perform a recovery attack.[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/35408ab01132edee84105a5a1a1c2b3aa8445784.png[/img]
[h2]Advanced Combat
[/h2]
These are Skills that amplify various parts of your Class. It could be related to specific combos, could add additional moves to the kit that are specific to the class (new move, variation of a move, etc). This is where a lot of build crafting comes from.
[list]
[*] Eviscerating Lift: Inflict Bleed (4s) after executing the Advanced Light Combo (YXXXX). Bleed: deals medium damage twice per second
[*] Bloodlust: Sword attacks deal 10% more damage againts Bleeding enemies.
[*] Sanguine Burst: Heavy Combo Finisher (YYY) consumes all Bleed stacks on the enemy, triggering an explosion. Each stack of Bleed increases the explosion damage by 5%.
[*] Sanguine Assault: Exploding 5 or more stacks of Bleed grants Prickly Strikes (5s) to self and all allies. Cooldown: 30s Prickly Strikes: Inflict Bleed (4s) per hit Bleed: deals medium damage twice per second
[*] Last Stand: When reaching Critical HP (25% or lower), grant self and all allies Aegis and Protection (8s). Cooldown: 30s Aegis: Negates the next incoming hit Protection: Damage taken -25%
[*] Vanguard: Increase DEF by 10% while Protection is active. Protection: Damage taken -25%
[*] Revival Ward: Gain Aegis (9s) while Reviving an ally. Cooldown: 10s Aegis: Negates the next incoming hit
[*] Guardbreaker: Shield attacks deal +15% Break Bar DMG.
[*] Shield Bash: Shield attacks have a 6% chance to inflict Stun (2s). Stun: Prevents movement and action
[*] Guardian's Rebound: Automatically Parry incoming enemy attacks while using Shield Attacks.
[*] Shatter-bash: Inflict Weakness (5s) after executing the Advanced Heavy Combo (XYYY). Weakness: -25% DMG
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/18cea1c8110f33dcb26fb0159dece9438acaa010.png[/img]
[h2]Focus Skills
[/h2]Every weapon boasts a roster of high-impact techniques that consume Focus, a meter earned through skillful play. Equip any two outside combat, then unleash them mid-fight to redefine the encounter. Mixing and matching these abilities lets you tailor burst damage, crowd control, or mobility to the mission at hand. For the Sentinel, here is a sampling of the Focus Abilities you can choose from. 

[i]Your [b]Light Focus Skills[/b] are your 1 bar focus skills. Uses LT + Light Attack to activate. You can only have one of these. Your [b]Heavy Focus Skills[/b] are your 2 bar focus skills. Uses LT + Heavy Attack to activate. You can only have one of these. [/i]
[h3]Light Focus
[/h3]
[list]
[*] Dashing Skewer: Press LT+X to lunge forward, dealing damage to enemies and inflicting Bleed (4s). Break Bar DMG: Low
[*] Radiant Guard: Press LT+X to raise the shield, emitting a burst of light and inflicting Stun (3s) on nearby enemies. This attack is Unblockable and can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High
[*] Reeling Spin: Press LT+X to spin in place 3 times, pulling in all nearby enemies and dealing damage. Break Bar DMG: Low
[/list][h3]Heavy Focus
[/h3]
[list]
[*] Steady Strikes: Press LT+Y to execute a quick flurry of 7 slashes, dealing damage and staggering enemies hit. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High
[*] Shield Rush: Press LT+Y to charge forward with the shield raised, striking all enemies in the path. This attack Block Breaks and can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High
[*] Crownbreaker: Press LT+Y to leap up and drive the shield into the ground. Deals damage and Launches surrounding enemies. This attack can be used while Airborne. Break Bar DMG: High
[/list]

notes.title: One-Time Progress Reset, Explained
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/09b44250b980d60e801638b88c5a5c03014e1ce7.png[/img]
[i]Hey, Aces - 

[/i]The one-and-only reset (aka wipe) arrives on April 29 - simultaneously with[url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2458830?emclan=103582791473758636&emgid=802308936293157007] Update 6[/url]. Resetting progression this one time is a key step to delivering the best possible experience for every player across every platform.  We will be uniting players via cross-play and progression with a clean slate on Xbox, WinPC, and Steam. 

This is a one-time reset which will impact only those who've played Towerborne before 04.29 (via Steam). If you’re joining us fresh on Xbox / Game Pass or Windows PC, your journey begins new and uninterrupted—there will be no future wipes beyond this one!

[h2]What Does this Mean for Me?[/h2]
[i][h3]What Resets, What Stays
[/h3][/i]
If you're already playing as a Towerborne Founder on Steam, this reset will directly impact your current progress.
[b]
Resets for Towerborne Steam Founders on April 29 
[/b][list][*] Class Level
[*] Progression: World Map, Danger Level, and Quests
[*] Inventory: Weapons, Gear, Aspects, Umbra, and Resources
[*] Writs
[/list][b]Kept through the reset
[/b][list][*] Ace Rank
[*] All Cosmetics, Emotes, Stickers
[*] Unlocked Curios and unused Curio Cores
[/list]
[h2]What to Expect Going Forward
[/h2]

First of all … will there be any more resets? No! This is the first, last, and only one! :) 

On April 29 every Towerborne player will have access to Update 6, which will bring cross-play and cross progression across all platforms going forward. You can expect new class skills, a map and mission overhaul (and expansion), tons of gameplay and systems improvements, and even more ways to customize your playstyle and your Ace style.

We're so thankful for your trust, support, patience, and feedback so far. And we've been delighted by the camaraderie and connection already felt throughout our growing community - so for you veteran Aces out there, get ready to grab a rookie Founder and show 'em the ropes! 

Whether you're an OG Founder or freshly joining our ranks … gear up, things are about to get even better.

notes.title: Towerborne Cross Platform Play Lands on April 29!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/88899dac6fe2670dc5a2e4ef1e3cc0164fe67cd0.png[/img]

[i]Greetings, Aces (and soon-to-be Aces),[/i]

Big news: on April 29, Towerborne is bringing some big game changes - including officially arriving on [b]Xbox Game Preview and Game Pass[/b] - you'll be able to play Towerborne on Xbox Series X|S, Windows PC via the Xbox app.

Last September, we kicked off in Steam Early Access and we’ve taken big steps forward thanks to your feedback. Update 6: Class Mastery drops April 29, brining a reimagined World Map (tons more missions) and—you guessed it—a way deeper Class Mastery system. Oh, and we'll be expanding to a new platform, too!
[previewyoutube=dXcJ-rpT8Dg;full][/previewyoutube]

Update 6: Class Mastery will get us a big step closer to making good on our ambition: to deliver a new kind of robust, replayable Looter Brawler experience. Here’s the rundown of what Xbox Game Preview will mean for Towerborne:
[list]

[*][b]Towerborne’s cross play and progression system[/b] is one of the key things that will be rolling out; Towerborne is an Xbox Play Anywhere title—meaning your progress, gear, and friends carry seamlessly across Xbox and PC, no matter where you jump in. Xbox Game Preview allows us to keep fine-tuning the game on our path to our full 1.0 launch later this year. 

[*][b]To be clear, this isn’t our full, official 1.0 launch just yet[/b]—but it IS a massive leap forward. More worlds to uncover, more skills to master, more loot to snag, and way [b]more[/b] ways to customize the way you look-and-play.
[/list]
Get ready to squad up, jump in, and help shape as we move ever closer toward our official full launch later this year! And if you can’t wait until then (we totally get it), stop what you’re doing and grab a Founder’s Pack on Steam today and play via Steam Early Access.

[h2]What to Expect with Towerborne’s Next Big Update[/h2]

To whet your appetite, here’s a brief, high-level overview of what to expect with [b]Update 6: Class Mastery[/b]...

[list]
[*][b]Couch Co-op Lands on Xbox![/b] Grab a controller, rally your crew, and dive into the deliciously nostalgic chaos of classic local couch co-op button mashing goodness...

[*][b]Cross-Platform Play & Progression[/b]: Team up effortlessly across Xbox and PC - [i]including Steam[/i]. Keep your gear, friends, and progress intact everywhere you play.

[*][b]All-New Class Skills[/b]: Earn Skill Points, unlock game-changing Focus Skills, customize your Ace’s mechanics, and freely adjust your build between missions to master every challenge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/5b24125797f214d08fcec51efbbcf1838e8f32aa.png[/img]

[*][b]Reimagined World & Missions[/b]: Embark on over 50 handcrafted new missions, a more engaging questline, and excitingly repositioned boss battles for a smoother, richer adventure.

[*][b]Fresh Loot, Allies & Fierce Enemies[/b]: Powerful new Legendary items await, enhancing your Focus Skills. Plus, two new Umbra allies—Boshi and Querida—join your side, and the fearsome Merk Brawler enemy arrives to test your strength.

[*][b]Leveled Up Social Play[/b]: For the next update, we’ve tuned up our in-game utility [b]Group Finder[/b] for quick matchmaking by mission type. Your Friends List sorting and online status indicator will be clearer and you’ll also be able to invite Aces and squad up directly from the Belfry or World Map.

[*][b]Quality-of-Life Upgrades[/b]:

[list]
[*][b]Mender’s Flask[/b]: Lives are gone—heal proactively mid-combat instead.
[*][b]Aspect Overhaul[/b]: Enhanced item customization for deeper strategic personalization.
[*][b]Improved Request Board[/b]: Greater variety, more daily jobs, and streamlined tracking.
[*][b]Remappable Keybinds & Item Badging[/b]: Personalize your control scheme and easily track newly-acquired items.
[/list]
[/list]From the start- we set out to make a one-of-a-kind Looter Brawler experience—melding the tried and true side-scrolling brawler combat we know and love with the rewarding loot and customization of an action RPG. Founder feedback has (and will continue to) help us pave the path to ship our full 1.0 launch later this year – join the community conversation on [url=https://discord.gg/towerborne]DIscord[/url] to stay up to date.

In the meantime, OG Steam Early Access Founders ... prepare for many more Aces to join the Founder ranks on April 29!

notes.title: Courage’s Time Trial: Outlast the Onslaught!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/6bbb526e85f80e37072771fba7102cf9b5a2cb10.png[/img][i]Ready, set …[/i]  

Grab your gear and your combat swagger - Courage’s Time Trial mode is here: waves of enemies, a relentless ticking clock, and the glory (and gear) you’ll earn [i]if you can last …  [/i]

[previewyoutube=nTkBuMmM-8c;full][/previewyoutube]

What rewards are at stake, you ask? Well, you can farm loot all you want by rinsing and repeating – but also, Courage’s temporally tedious task is also a chance at some rare cosmetics - in honor of Courage himself.  
[hr][/hr]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/f94b7985b558088c9c767ef8f5437c59f2c89170.png[/img]

[i]Why just wield courage when you can wear it, too?[/i]
[hr][/hr]
Notably, this is the first time you can earn cosmetics as a loot drop!  

Here's how rewards work per each Trial:  
[list]  
[*][b]Earn chests[/b] by progressing through waves of monsters. The further you progress, the better the chests.  
[*][b]Make it to the end, get a final chest[/b] with even better rewards (based on your score).  
[*][b]Hard Mode ups the stakes[/b] - and ups your chances to reap better rewards.  
[/list]  
New challenge. New (Time Trial) buffs. And more loot. What more could you ask for? Well, besides a breather; but you won’t get that here. Time Trial mode will be available for two weeks - starting from [i]right now[/i] … Dive in before, well, time runs out …  

[h2]The Basics[/h2]  

Your mission: survive endless waves of enemies while racking up points before the clock hits zero. Every kill gets you points, and quick kills in succession stack up your multiplier for bonus scores. But stall out—hesitate for just a few seconds—and that multiplier is toast.  

What's better than testing your skills while you race against the clock? Why, doing it with friends, of course! To jump into [b]Courage’s Time Trial[/b] – gather your group and check in with Courage, the Belfry’s boisterous battlefield mentor. Accept the Quest, and get ready for the action—once you start, the timer ticks down as you face waves of baddies.  

This mode is live from [b]Feb 25 8am Pacific to March 11 8am Pacific.[/b]

Think you’ve got what it takes to triumph in Courage’s Time Trial? Not so fast, Ace - first, you need to make sure to do the following:  

[list]  
[*]Make sure you've completed the essential, early quest, “[b]A Return to Form[/b]” – which is your gateway to unlocking Danger Level 2 (DL2), granting you access to the map, and to the job board. You don't need to have completed any curios to have access.  

[*]When you’re ready to jump into [b]Time Trial Mode[/b] (and you’ve met the prerequisites) - first, go check in with [b]Courage[/b], your ever-enthusiastic battlefield mentor and accpet the Time Trials Quest. Second, interact with one of the training dummies to then jump into the game mode. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/f992a35dfb8017e984228ab1b4564d9b3fa1e7a6.png[/img]
[*]Now you’re in the thick of it. The timer ticks down as you face waves of enemies … smash hourglasses to scrounge up extra seconds, grab buffs to better your battling, and stay alive to secure that sweet, sweet loot! 
[/list]  
[h2]The Details[/h2]  

Fight with flair, finesse, and just a dash of desperation. Here’s a quick overview video of how Time Trial mode works.  

[previewyoutube=FMGa8H8lv38;full][/previewyoutube]
[list][*][b]Time is Your Nemesis:[/b] Tick…tick…tick… –what are you waiting for?! Those waves of baddies aren’t going to slay themselves. Defeat enemies, grab buffs, smash hourglasses to stave off the buzzer. Every second counts, and one wrong move can leave you with nothing but regrets.  
[*][b]New! Buff Shrines:[/b] Mid-run, [i]Buff Shrines[/i] will appear, offering powerful pick-me-ups for you and your squad. Want to hit harder? Move faster? Wield lightning strikes with just a jump (for real)? Choose wisely—pick one buff, and the rest disappear!  
[*][b]Dial Up the Danger:[/b] Choose your difficulty: Easy, Medium, or Hard. Got the *courage* to take on the ultimate challenge? Try Hard Mode. We dare you.  
[*][b]Slay Swiftly to Score:[/b] Keep those kills coming to rack up multipliers—but hesitate too long, and your score resets. Speed and precision are your only allies here.  
[*][b]Conquer the Clock, Claim Your Prize:[/b] Complete Courage’s quests to earn the (new) Courage gear set (among a bunch more loot) - so you can show off your Time Trial conquering prowess. The better you do, the better the loot!  
[/list]  
[h2]Buff Up or Bow Out (SPOILERS AHEAD)[/h2]  

Consider the following details to count as game mode spoilers, a warning for those who’d rather take a crack at a Time Trial first and come back when you have an itch for more details.  

But for you doomsday preppers out there - read on!
[spoiler]  
Shrines are your sanctuary - and now, also your secret weapon. They appear after certain waves and offer you buffs that can mean the difference between glory and failure. Each Shrine forces you to make a choice—pick the buff that suits your playstyle, and hope it’s enough to keep you alive.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/903d5472e77c8d1fc6be09758659294494d83f39.png[/img]

If you’re rolling with fellow Aces - remember: first Ace to choose a buff, that buff is then applied to everyone.  

[b]Permanent Buffs:[/b] Boost your health, increase damage, add crit chance, and more. These last the entire match.  
[list]  
[*]**Max Power Increase** – Adds 1 bar of Focus.  
[*]**Max Health Boost** – Increases health by 500 HP.  
[*]**Max Umbra Increase** – Adds +1 to Umbra Charge.  
[*]**Full Health Restore** – Instantly restores all health.  
[*]**Damage Boost** – Increases damage output by 15%.  
[*]**Critical Hit Chance Up** – Increases crit chance by 10%.  
[/list]  
[b]Temporary Buffs:[/b] Short bursts of power, like explosive dodges, poison attacks, or lightning-infused jumps. Use them wisely—they don’t stick around long.  
[list]  
[*]**Time Boost** – Grants +25 seconds on the timer.  
[*]**Damage Surge** – Increases Might for 45 seconds.  
[*]**Explosive Dodge** – Dodging causes an explosion (30 seconds).  
[*]**Fire Attacks** – Attacks inflict fire damage (45 seconds).  
[*]**Critical Strike Boost** – Increases critical hit chance (30 seconds).  
[*]**Lightning Dash** – Dashing triggers a lightning strike (45 seconds).  
[/list][/spoiler]  
I mean, I know we’re just talking about practice … but those rewards aren’t going to win themselves. Fight fast, or fail. Those are your only two options. And, don’t forget - like everything in Towerborne - glorious chaos is better with friends! 

Definitely join us on Discord for plenty of boasting and battle strategy … share your winning scores and tactics for thwarting the clock! Your feedback will go into making Time Trial mode that much more exciting going forward.  

Time waits for no one … see you out there, Aces!

notes.title: Key Bindings Blunder (Sorry!)
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/fb397cf30ea0377d8fa5058b9c8a312b5175f27b.png[/img]

Greetings, Aces -  

So, in our last update, we fumbled the ball on custom key bindings, which messed things up for folks who play with keyboard-only. Yikes! That wasn’t part of the plan—you know it, we know it. We understand the frustration for any of you dealing with it, and we want to apologize!  

Here’s an explanation, and a stop-gap solution:  

[h2]What’s different?[/h2]

The [b]keyboard-only, play without a “.ini” file tweak is no longer possible …[/b]  

Basically, before the most recent update, you could play Towerborne with keyboard and mouse / keyboard-only without having to do anything special. However, right now, you can't play keyboard-only, without taking a particular action.  

Here’s the context:  
[list]
[*] We’re preparing to deploy an in-client key rebinding solution. When we do, the [i]current[/i] method of editing your “.ini” files will go away.  
[*] We unintentionally shipped the updated bindings that removed keyboard-only controls. [b]Our bad![/b]  
[*] This is totally on us – we’re sorry, and please know that we’ll push an update when we can to bring back the original keybinds.  
[/list]  
[b]To be clear, you can still push through keyboard-only controls [i]manually[/i] … see below to get the right file and check out our older post for instructions.[/b]  

-----
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/a09a10392a45569eb8f7494bf50988bfb9ab3801.png[/img]
[i]Caption: The buttons you change do actually appear in the HUD now. Except for Light Focus Skill and Heavy Focus Skill, which end up looking super weird for some reason.[/i]  
-----

In a future release, we will be updating the game so you can edit *in-game* (and this file will be changed).  

Here’s what’s different from before the last update:  
[list]
[*] [b]F is now Interact.[/b] This used to be E.  
[*] [b]Q is now Focus Skill 1.[/b] This used to be X.  
[*] [b]E is now Focus Skill 2.[/b] This used to be C.  
[/list]  
[h2]How do I manually remap my controls?[/h2]  

Right now, we’re unable to revert the change immediately ourselves – but you [b]can[/b] update things manually as a stopgap.  

The original **instructions for manually remapping keys** can be found [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2458830/view/6516237014665441026]here in their thorough glory[/url] (our original post)... we highly recommend checking that out for a step-by-step guide. Also, here’s a handy [url=https://youtu.be/WRqfbw3YVas]YouTube walkthrough[/url], too.

[h3]Remapping Controls - An Overview / Refresher[/h3]

(1) - [b]Find the Game Files[/b] – In Steam, right-click Towerborne, go to [i]Manage[/i] > Browse Local Files, then open the [i]Belfry[/i] folder.

(2) - [b]Create a Config File[/b] – Inside [i]Belfry[/i], create a [i]Config[/i] folder.

(3) - [b]Drag and drop[/b] your “UserInput.ini” file into the [i]Config[/i] folder (you need “Show File Extensions” enabled - check out step by step instructions for more).

[b]Here are the ".ini" files[/b] you’ll need, depending on the control scheme you’re interested in – download, unzip, and drag-and-drop your “UserInput.ini” file into the [i]Config[/i] folder (you need “Show File Extensions” enabled - check out [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2458830/view/6516237014665441026]step by step instructions[/url] for more).

[*] [url=https://www.towerborne.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/UserInput_KBM.zip]Default Keyboard and Mouse controls[/url] (from before most recent update)  
[*] [url=https://www.towerborne.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/UserInput_KO.zip]Default Keyboard-only controls[/url] (from before most recent update)  

[i]Edit the Controls (if you want!)[/i] – Open UserInput.ini, change keys as needed, save, and launch the game.  

Thanks for sticking with us, and as always, keep the feedback coming—we're listening!  

[previewyoutube=WRqfbw3YVas;full][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Early Access: Update 5 - Combat & Balance Tuning
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/251176243a3990f7f82064840efa45a83a59eaa7.png[/img]

[i]Greetings, Aces![/i]

While we continue to get after it to build bigger and better – we’re keeping the ball rolling in this small-but-mighty update with cleaner combat, sharper balance, and a few pesky bugs retired. Enemy attacks are a little fairer, abilities feel a little snappier, and your gear should be working just the way it should.

This update might look smaller on the surface, but it’s laying the groundwork for what’s next. Most of the player-facing changes are about tuning and fixes, but behind the scenes, Update 5 is doing a lot of heavy lifting. Without it, some of the bigger things we’ve got in the pipeline wouldn’t be possible. So hang in there—we’ve got more coming soon, and we think you’re going to be excited about what’s next.

In the meantime, check out this update’s deets, below!

… and, later this month - we've got a cool new mode built to test your strength and skills and most of all - speed. We’re putting the finishing touches on it as we speak…just needs a little more time⏳ 

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Gameplay & Exploration[/h2]
This update keeps things running smoother with balance tweaks, tuning, and groundwork for what's next—setting the stage for future content.
[list]
[*][b]Items[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Somewhat increased base ATK and DEF values when upgrading items past Level 50.
    [*]Exploding Mushroom hazards dropped by [i]The Fumigator[/i] legendary now have different coloring than normal Exploding Mushroom hazards.
    [*]Fixed a bug with [i]Wildling’s Sword[/i] where it now drops with the correct Focus Gain stat.
    [*][i]Feral’s Bane[/i] legendary daggers will now drop with the ATK stat instead of DEF stat. Only applies to items acquired post-update.
    [*][i]The Northern Inferno[/i] legendary warclub will now drop with the Weapon Meter Gain stat instead of Burn Resistance. Only applies to items acquired post-update.
    [/list][*][b]Settings Update[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Player settings preferences are now linked to accounts rather than devices.
    [/list][*][b]Job Board[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Job board quests requiring players to play missions with a specific Umbra equipped now require players to use specific Umbra skills during missions.
    [/list][/list][h2]Combat[/h2]
This update fine-tunes combat across the board—smoother attacks, better responsiveness, and adjustments that make every fight feel tighter and more fluid.
[h3]Classes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Rockbreaker[/b]
    [list]
    [*]YXXX Combo Finisher now hits 13 frames earlier.
    [/list][*][b]Shadowstriker[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Fixed an issue where the Dash Light Combo Finisher was missing a Dodge Cancel window.
    [/list][*][b]Pyroclast[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Various improvements to the feel of attacks. In general, attacks should still feel weighty but are technically faster than before. It’s largely subtle but it makes a difference!
    [/list][/list][h3]Umbra[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]McKraken[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Adjusted animation start-up time so that it feels more in line with other Umbra.
    [*]Increased Focus Meter generation rate… have fun!
    [/list][*][b]Morberry[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Adjusted animation start-up time so that it feels more in line with other Umbra.
    [/list] [/list][h3]Enemies[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]General[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Visual tells have been improved for a variety of enemies. Many Lieutenants now have added recovery tells or start-up tells for their unique attacks.
    [*]Visual improvements have been made to the Break Bar recovery moment. Enemies have more obvious tells before the burst occurs.
    [/list][*][b]Ratslasher[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Added a visual tell to the 3rd hit of its combo chain so that it’s easier to identify that it block breaks and that it’s not a true combo.
    [*]This is an attack that is meant to be evaded midway through even on hit. This moment should be more obvious now.
    [/list][*][b]Quivertail[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Adjusted hitboxes on Opportunity Attack so that it better matches the visual of the animation.
    [/list][*][b]Merk Marauder[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Fixed an issue where the offscreen indicator was in the wrong position.
    [/list][*][b]Boarealis Stoutswine[/b]
    [list]
    [*]Slightly lowered frequency of Boar Rush charge attack.
    [/list]
[/list]

notes.title: Early Access: Update 4, Patch 1 - Balancing and Bug Fixing
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/4cb634de7163ce21144a3c1744dda6ba1c5db455.png[/img][i]Greetings, Aces,[/i]

With this update, Grandeur may be officially over … what’s that you say? What about all those Grandeur Writs you’ve accumulated? Don’t fret – you may have noticed, as a gallant gesture of Grandeur gratitude, that all your Grandeur Writs have magically transformed into regular Writs—ensuring nothing goes to waste!

Here’s a breakdown of what’s been updated:

[h2]Gameplay & Exploration[/h2]

- [b]Grandeur Event Curio Removed and Writs Converted[/b]: Grandeur Writs were supposed to be retired - so they won’t be available going forward … but don’t fret! All of your Grandeur Writs have now been converted to regular ‘ol writs, ensuring you can still enjoy the fruits of your Grandeur labor.

- [b]Beta Label Removed[/b]: Some players may have noticed the word “Beta” in the bottom left of the title screen - that’s been removed.

[h2]Combat[/h2]

- [b]Focus Gain Affix Fixed[/b]: Resolved a bug where the "Focus Gain" attribute was doubling its intended value, causing balance issues. You can now expect accurate scaling when equipping gear with this attribute. Additionally, fixed an issue where repeatedly equipping and unequipping "Focus Gain" items caused misleading Focus Gain stat increases (it was a visual bug, stats weren’t actually affected; the visual bug has been fixed).

notes.title: Early Access: Update 4 - New Missions & Languages
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/ba7780266fa7bdbbcf335543e5ff2eb1404d6c7a.png[/img]
[i]Greetings, Aces![/i]

Happy 2025! Our first update of the year is here—bringing exciting new updates, including mission types and map improvements, expanded language support, and a special perk for Founders: the ability to claim all previous Monthly Bonuses.

Kicking things off, the World Map will feature three new mission types. Each can be completed once, and some have graduated from discovery tiles to permanent spots on the map. Beyond that, we’ve fine-tuned combat and enemy behaviors, and polished up the visuals (no more NPCs mysteriously losing their faces—oops!). Enemies now have sharper responses and clearer tells, making fights challenging but fair. Plus, this update brings some love to your inventory, tweaks to item stats, and improved mission flow to keep things moving.

What’s that you say? More-monster-mangling was your New Year’s Resolution, too?! Well, then—what are you waiting for? Ready up, Aces … this year is gonna be a doozy.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]More Languages[/h2]
The Belfry continues to welcome Aces from around the world with these new options, bringing our support language count to 23:
[list]
[*]Polish (pl-PL)
[*]Danish (da-DK)
[*]Swedish (sv-SE)
[*]Norwegian (nb-NO)
[*]Finnish (fi-FI)
[/list][h2]Gameplay & Exploration[/h2]
This update hits some quality-of-life love for your inventory, item balancing fun, tweaks to mission and progression flow, and more. Dive in and see what’s new!

[h3]Founders: Claim Past Monthly Bonuses![/h3]
[list]
[*]With this update, Founders can now claim all previous Monthly Founder Bonuses—no more Ace envy for you newer Aces out there!
[/list][h3]New Mission Types[/h3]
Three new types of missions can be found on the World Map. Each one of these missions can be completed once. Some of these missions used to appear in discovery tiles, but now have a permanent location on the map. These were missions like escorting the wagon or helping the City of Number refugees as they try to make their way to the Belfry.
[list]
[*][b]Guide and Guard[/b] - Protect or escort wagons.
[*][b]Bait and Clear[/b] - New challenging missions where players progress through waves of enemies by ringing a bell.
[*][b]Chance Encounter[/b] - Unique experiences for the Ace to discover (Some of these you may have come across in a discovery mission before, but there are also new encounters and missions to discover).
[/list][h3]Quality of Life Improvements[/h3]
[b]Easier Group Finder Access[/b]
[list]
[*]You now don’t have to go back to the Belfry to access Group Finder; find your group from the World Map, too! 
[/list][b]Storage Increase[/b]
[list]
[*]Increased the Aspect inventory storage limit from 50 to 80, to match the Weapon and Gear storage limits.
[/list][b]Loot Adjustments[/b]
[list]
[*]Improved the drop rates for many Legendary items that were rarer than intended.
[*]Adjusted loot throughout the game to bias slightly in favor of gear dropping over weapons.
[/list][b]Item Stats Balance[/b]
[list]
[*]Strike DMG min/max random substat values reduced.
[*]Umbra Strength min/max random substat values increased.
[*]The “Focus Gain When Hit” item stat is now considered a Legacy stat. It will still function on existing items with this stat, but will no longer appear on newly acquired items.
[*]Its functionality has been rolled into the “Focus Gain on Hit” stat, which has now been relabeled to “Focus Gain.”
[*]Changed the static substats of the “Cambulary’s Strength” Legendary Sword:
   [list]
   [*]Bleed DMG → DMG Reduction
   [*]Crit DMG → Strike DMG
   [*]Existing Cambulary’s Strength items will be considered legacy items and retain their original affixes.
   [/list][*]Changed one of the static substats of the “Red Handed” Legendary Gauntlets:
   [list]
   [*]Crit DMG → Health Per Hit
[*]Existing Red Handed items will be considered legacy items and retain their original affixes.
   [/list][*]Crit DMG is now calculated as a multiplicative modifier rather than additive. It will now stack as expected with other damage modifiers like Strike DMG.
[list]
[/list][/list][h3]Tech Tweaks[/h3]
[list]
[*]You can now scan a unique QR code in the Settings Menu to reach the ticket submission page to receive support.
[*]Various network stability fixes.
[*]Improved framerate while navigating menus.
[*]Fixed an issue with incorrect player profiles being shown.
[/list][h3]Mission & Progression Adjustments[/h3]
[list]
[*]The conversation screen that displayed “I don’t have anything for you right now” has been removed. The screen will now close if an NPC doesn’t have any new conversations. If you interact with an NPC that doesn’t have any conversations, a menu will display indicating no conversations are available.
[*]After loading into a mission, the quest tracker now hides itself after a couple of seconds. The information can still be brought back up by pressing [b]2[/b] on the keyboard or [b]RIGHT arrow[/b] on controller.
[*]Fixed a bug with Danger License Trials not displaying health bars correctly, and reinforcement enemies not spawning.
[*]Adjustments have been made to how encounters are selected in discovery missions, resulting in a more varied experience.
[*]Discovery missions now have a more contained selection of enemies.
[*]Numbers Ironworks background art was updated.
[/list][h2]Combat[/h2]
[h3]Classes[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Sentinel[/b]: Fixed an issue where certain Combo Finishers were not tagged properly.
[*][b]Pyroclast[/b]: Fixed an issue where certain Combo Finishers were not tagged properly.
[*][b]Rockbreaker[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused a Level 1 Powderkeg Punch to hit later than expected.
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused a Level 3 Powderkeg Punch to fire automatically while charging when paired with certain Aspects.
   [*]Adjusted the visual language of Skyward Swing’s vortex to improve gameplay visibility.
   [/list][*][b]Shadowstriker[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused Sunrise Shrapnel to have a smaller hitbox than intended.
   [*]Adjusted the hitbox on Dash Light Attack so that it hits more reliably.
   [*]Air Heavy Attack, when used as a Combo Finisher, is now properly counted as a Finisher.
   [/list][/list][h3]Umbra[/h3]
[list]
[*][b]Sten[/b]: Adjusted commit window so that you’re less likely to lose a charge if interrupted during the cast animation.
[*][b]Picus[/b]: Fixed an issue that caused airborne enemies to not get put into the proper hit reaction.
[*][b]Grimel[/b]: Adjusted cancel window timing so that you can do combos more intuitively.
[/list]
[h2]Enemies[/h2]
Your foes just got a little smarter—and fairer! This update polishes enemy behavior, improves visual cues, and makes fights smoother without losing the challenge.
[list]
[*][b]Break Bar[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Enemies now have a much more obvious animation tell when they’re about to reactivate their Break Bar after being stunned.
   [*]Adjusted hitbox of reactivate shockwave so that it feels less sudden when it hits the Ace.
   [/list][*][b]Enrage[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Enemies now have a much more obvious animation tell when they’re about to activate Enrage. Enrage now hits on frame 60 instead of frame 25.
   [*]Lowered Break Bar HP for fodder enemies, making it easier to break them, which deactivates the Enrage state.
   [/list]
[/list][h3]Enemy Adjustments[/h3]
[list][*][b]Flickertail[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Adjusted landing frames from the Leapshot so that it’s easier to punish on whiff.
   [*]Adjusted movement behavior to alleviate an issue where Flickertail walked backwards more often than intended.
   [*]Adjusted the hitboxes of the Smoke Bomb projectiles so that they’re more reflective of the visual.
   [*]Adjusted Flaming Sky Arrows so that there is a visual tell that signals their landing positions.
   [/list][*][b]Gobo Brute[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Adjusted cooldowns to improve the pacing of the fight.
   [*]Added a new attack tell to the dashing Heavy Attack so that it’s less abrupt in gameplay.
   [*]Added missing Block Breaker warning visual to the dashing Heavy Attack.
   [*]Adjusted the hitbox of the dashing Heavy Attack so that it better reflects the swipe visual.
   [/list][*][b]Gobo Tailwhipper[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused the Tailwhipper to not go into a proper reaction when Parried.
   [/list][*][b]Merk Marauder[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]The running Charge Attack has been adjusted so that it only causes a Stun when the Marauder is Enraged.
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused the Flipping Double Axe Attack to hit earlier than intended.
   [/list][*][b]Merk Slugger & Conscript[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Adjusted attack cooldowns to better pace their combat actions and alleviate frustration.
   [*]Adjusted attack ownership so that the Ace doesn’t get put into repeated hitstun reactions in quick succession.
   [/list][*][b]Dusker Nightmare[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused Parry VFX to not appear correctly.
   [/list][*][b]Dusker[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused Parry VFX to not appear correctly.
   [/list][*][b]The Shepherd[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Fixed an issue that caused Parry VFX to not appear correctly.
   [/list][*][b]Yxil[/b]:
   [list]
   [*]Adjusted hitboxes of ground projectiles so that it’s easier to jump over them.
   [*]Fixed a bug that caused the Ground Stab visuals to appear underneath the ground instead of on top of the ground.
   [*]Adjusted the timing of the stab so that it pops out from the ground 10 frames later. It also has a longer visual warning to help players anticipate the attack.
   [/list]
[/list][h2]UI/UX[/h2]
We’ve spruced up the interface so it’s smoother. Plus, we added some audio flair and squashed a few bugs—because no one likes those.
[list]
[*]Fixed multiple danger license-related layout bugs in various languages.
[*]Added keyboard scrolling in popups.
[*]Improved readability of pinned quest text.
[*]Added a warning when purchasing a cosmetic when the base item is not yet owned.
[*]Fixed layout of Ace rank and name in the group tab.

[*]Fixed layout of challenge timer in cases where it could become obstructed.
[*]Added an audio cue when starting a DLT.
[*]Fixed points in the store where the scroll bar could disappear.
[*]Fixed the mark-mode in the forge not letting players swap tabs.
[/list]
[h2]Art[/h2]
Bug fixing on the Art front should sharpen up your visual experience while making sure NPCs are looking their best. Enjoy!
[list]
[*]Fixed a Z-fighting issue in the Rescue Husband Event in the Mountains Biome.
[*]Fixed an issue where a Tower NPC was missing facial features.

[/list]

The Belfry continues to welcome Aces from around the world with these new options, bringing our support language count to 23:

[/list]
With this update, Founders can now claim all previous Monthly Founder Bonuses—no more Ace envy for you newer Aces out there!

Three new types of missions can be found on the World Map. Each one of these missions can be completed once. Some of these missions used to appear in discovery tiles, but now have a permanent location on the map. These were missions like escorting the wagon or helping the City of Number refugees as they try to make their way to the Belfry.
[list]
[*][b]Guide and Guard[/b] - Protect or escort wagons.
[*][b]Bait and Clear[/b] - New challenging missions where players progress through waves of enemies by ringing a bell.
[*][b]Chance Encounter[/b] - Unique experiences for the Ace to discover (Some of these you may have come across in a discovery mission before, but there are also new encounters and missions to discover).
[/list]
You now don’t have to go back to the Belfry to access Group Finder; find your group from the World Map, too!

tags.balance_change: Increased the Aspect inventory storage limit from 50 to 80, to match the Weapon and Gear storage limits.
Improved the drop rates for many Legendary items that were rarer than intended.
Adjusted loot throughout the game to bias slightly in favor of gear dropping over weapons.
Strike DMG min/max random substat values reduced.
Umbra Strength min/max random substat values increased.

The “Focus Gain When Hit” item stat is now considered a Legacy stat. It will still function on existing items with this stat, but will no longer appear on newly acquired items.
Its functionality has been rolled into the “Focus Gain on Hit” stat, which has now been relabeled to “Focus Gain.”

Changed the static substats of the “Cambulary’s Strength” Legendary Sword:
   [list]
   [*]Bleed DMG → DMG Reduction
   [*]Crit DMG → Strike DMG
   [*]Existing Cambulary’s Strength items will be considered legacy items and retain their original affixes.

Changed one of the static substats of the “Red Handed” Legendary Gauntlets:
   [list]
   [*]Crit DMG → Health Per Hit
[*]Existing Red Handed items will be considered legacy items and retain their original affixes.
   [/list]
Crit DMG is now calculated as a multiplicative modifier rather than additive. It will now stack as expected with other damage modifiers like Strike DMG.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/89046aad82d460370779be19b0883da9e94e964a.png[/img]
[i]Greetings, Aces![/i]

As the Belfry buzzes with festive cheer, there’s no better time to join your fellow Aces in defending humanity’s last stronghold… ICYMI, Towerborne Founder’s Packs are [b]20 percent off[/b] during the current Winter Sale ([b]Dec 19 - Jan 2[/b])!

And, while our special holiday “[i]12 Days of Grandeur[/i]” sticker giveaway may be coming to an end soon… the festive fun will stick around into the new year. It’s the perfect time to suit up, Ace rookies! … or, the perfect time to peer pressure your friends, Ace veterans! Grab a Founder’s pack and jump in!

[h3]8 days down, 4 to go…[/h3]
For those of you who’ve been amassing more stickers, good for you! Now you’ve got that many more ways to delight your friends, make them envious, or both. And for those of you who haven’t? Well, hey—you’ve got an entire third of the event left! Now’s the perfect time to snag some sticky gifts and start adventuring.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/22f764845891c61ac74b5592119c80068856bdf7.png[/img]

[h3]Git Some Writs While the Git’n is Good[/h3]
More gifts! In case you haven’t heard, we’ve increased the drop rate and amount of Grandeur Writs to make the celebration even grander! Grandeur Writs now drop at a higher rate and in more generous amounts.
[i]In case you need a refresher on seasonal Winter Writs, look no further![/i]
[list]
[*][b]What are Winter Writs?[/b]
Winter Writs are a limited-time currency available only during the Grandeur Event. You can use them to unlock exclusive seasonal cosmetics.

[*][b]How do you earn Winter Writs?[/b]
Complete the quest ‘A Grand Plan’, tackle the Aurora Ridge Venture, or finish standard challenges across the map.

[*][b]Can I earn more Winter Writs?[/b]
Yes! Playing at higher Danger Levels rewards more Writs.

[*][b]Do I need to replay ‘A Grand Plan’ to access Aurora Ridge?[/b]
No—‘A Grand Plan’ only needs to be completed once. After that, you can replay the Aurora Ridge Venture as many times as you like without redoing the quest.
[/list]
[h3]Deck Your Desktop Backgrounds with Boughs of Towerborne![/h3]
We've crafted a cadre of cozy and wintery wallpapers to wonder and delight. Check out a phone-background sample below - and [url=https://www.towerborne.com/media/]go to our media page and scroll to the bottom to find more wallpaper options[/url] for desktop and phone!

notes.title: Early Access: Update 3 - Grandeur
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/8807d60b0376c4f5f08d0dd23ad67e939f2b5f57.png[/img]

[i][h3]'Twas the Night Before Grandeur...[/h3]

...and all through the Tower,  
Fellow Aces were stirring—hey, there’s loot to be scoured!
... for Umbra were nestled in hues rainbow-bright,  
While mistle torches burned softly, lighting up the night.  

Bumble was quiet, his thoughts far away,  
Ogden had plans to bring joy to the day.  
“Take him to the mountains!” he said with a grin,  
“To witness the light shows and let Yuletide begin!”  

With Aces prepared and Bumble in tow,  
Through snow-covered trails, they braved the wild glow.  
To a bonfire of mistle they traveled with care,  
A gift from their friends—a spark to repair.  

High in the north, where the skies softly gleam,  
Bundles are burned, inspired by a dream.  
From mistle trees' branches and secretive lore,  
Families create hues that light up the shore.  

But beware, brave Aces, for Gobos abound,  
They’ve swapped bombs for brass bells with a jingling sound.  
Don’t be fooled—yes, their chimes may delight,  
Get close, and BOOM—it’ll end your good night!  

As furnaces roar and the Belfry stands tall,  
The season of Grandeur brings warmth to us all.  
Gather your allies, your quest is near—  
‘Tis the season to conquer this festive frontier![/i] 

[previewyoutube=0zoLdiC_PYM;full][/previewyoutube]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]The Big Picture...[/h1]

[i]Season’s Greetings, Aces! [/i]

With this update, we’re thrilled to unveil Towerborne’s December Update, [b]Grandeur[/b], decking the tower-halls with a wave of holiday magic! 

Enjoy the Belfry adorned with festive decorations while you embark on a delightful quest to help Bumble rekindle his holiday spirit. Don’t forget to partake in the “[b]12 Days of Grandeur[/b]” for daily sticker surprises. Plus, we’re excited to announce localization—Towerborne now supports 18 total languages to spread the love (and punching/stabbing/slicing/bludgeoning).  

As we continue our Early Access journey, Founder feedback remains essential in shaping Towerborne into something truly special. So please, keep the feedback coming! And in the meantime, jump into Grandeur and celebrate this festive season with us!  

[i]Here's what to expect...[/i]

[h2]Calling All Aces … From Around the World![/h2]
As winter winds swirl and festive lights glow in every corner, Towerborne is proudly throwing its doors open to adventurers far and wide. What’s the best gift we could give this season? A chance for more heroes, from more places, to join the party!  

Beyond English, you can now immerse yourself in heroic quests, playful banter, and rich storytelling in French, Italian, Latin American Spanish, Castilian Spanish, German, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Portuguese, Russian, Hungarian, Czech, Dutch, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, and Greek. Each language adds its own spark, uniting us beneath one tower, one banner, and one grand adventure.  

And we’re just getting started! As we march ever closer to our full release, expect even more languages and greater global accessibility. Together, we’re forging a worldwide community of heroes—because the only thing better than slaying monsters and snagging epic loot is doing it side by side, no matter where you call home. Your voice, your language, your adventure—let’s take on the world together!  

[h2]A Festive Fortress[/h2]
Experience the Belfry adorned with holiday-themed décor: rainbow smoke swirls from the Forge, gift boxes are tucked around every corner, and everyone’s rocking their best festive outfits. Even your Umbra buddies are sporting adorable holiday looks. It’s the perfect setting for seasonal adventures—whether it be lighting Mistle Torches or battling frustrating festive foes like Gobos tossing brass bell bombs and cold-hearted Snow Howlers.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/404c38003fdc9b2720b70f0f0a4a3abdf4acf7c9.png[/img]

[h2]A Grand Plan[/h2]
This update’s special, heartwarming quest will have you helping our favorite Forge overseer rekindle his holiday spirit. Accompany Bumble as you take a trip to the mountains—braving the rugged terrain and dodging brass bell bombs along the way. It’s times like these that the most fruitful festive-filled friendships are, well, forged. 

To start your Grandeur adventure, make sure you’ve completed the primary quest, “[b]A Writ of Passage[/b].” Then, head to Ogden in The Belfry at the Counsel Building to pick up the next quest, “[b]A Grand Plan[/b].”  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/d5f2b280dc820edc27a0e2699b62850d77643d9a.png[/img]

[h2]Holiday Cheer, Meet Holiday Gear[/h2]
What’s holiday cheer without some holiday gear? Get ready for a festive arsenal of gear sets, and weapons sure to send wintery shivers down those monster spines. Here's a sneak peek at what's in store, with the full list of details in notes below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/75037806609db11e3481e128173a11a1aef4510d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/56450bd5cc3d80444b9549e125ab64594be21f41.png[/img]

[h2]Seasonally Sticky Daily Gifts[/h2]
Join the “12 Days of Grandeur” and collect a daily surprise. Each day presents a new sticker to showcase your festive spirit in-game, adding a playful and creative touch to your character’s appearance. There are 12 stickers in all—check out a teaser of our first sticker below!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/435356604bda9ceae1a47bf81555480d3ccd9dd4.png[/img]

[hr][/hr]
[h1]The Details...[/h1]

[h2]Localization / Available Languages[/h2]
Towerborne now speaks your language—literally! From the buzzing streets of Berlin to the snowy peaks of the Alps … from Tokyo’s neon nights to the bustling markets of São Paulo … and a whole bunch of places in between—we’re welcoming Aces to suit up from all over the world.  

Play in 18 languages, including English, French, Italian, Latin American Spanish, Castilian Spanish, German, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese, Portuguese, Russian, Hungarian, Czech, Dutch, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Turkish, Japanese, and Greek. The Belfry is becoming a multi-lingual party—so pick your language, grab your controller/keyboard, and join a global adventure!

To select a preferred language, you have to change language directly within Towerborne’s in-game settings. Steam language settings do not carry over to the game.  

1. Go to [b]Settings > Accessibility > Language[/b].  
2. Scroll through the language options using the left or right arrow.  
3. Confirm your selection when prompted.  

[h2]Gameplay & Exploration[/h2]
Get ready to deck the halls—and some Gobos—with your fists! Grandeur brings not only holiday cheer but also a slew of gameplay and exploration updates to keep every journey fresh. From a festive new questline that sends you to snowy peaks to improved loot rewards, handy new settings, and even a quick return to the Belfry, there’s something for every adventurer this season. Embrace the season with the new questline, [b]A Grand Plan[/b] ... fire up that Grandeur bonfire … and enjoy holiday gear tweaks and the cozy feeling of a world evolving just for you!

[h3]Quality of Life & Mission Adjustments[/h3]

[b]New ‘Show Affix Roll Ranges’ Setting[/b]  
- Optionally allows the player to toggle on visibility of minimum and maximum values for randomized item stats. Found under [b]Settings > Gameplay > General[/b].  

[b]Loot Adjustments[/b]  
- Increased the number of Set Bonus Venture Gear items awarded from Venture end-of-mission chests by 1.  
- Somewhat increased the amount of Writs awarded from Venture end-of-mission chests at DL 3, 4, and 5.  
- Writs will no longer drop from Venture end-of-mission chests at DL 2.  

[b]Aspect of Dismantling Changes[/b]  
- Fixed a bug with the item name.  
- Increased the item's dismantle rewards from 80 → 140.  
- Converted the "Dismantle Me!" line into a perk, so it appears at the top of the item description in yellow text.  
- Replaced the +0 Health attribute with a randomly rolled substat.  

[b]Quality of Life Improvements[/b]  
- Updated the introduction mission so that NPC conversations can be progressed through interacting (skip to progress).  
- Players can now travel back to the Belfry from anywhere on the World Map by using the up arrow on the D-pad or "3" on the keyboard.  

[h3]A Grand(eur) ‘Ol Time[/h3]

[b]A New Questline: A Grand Plan[/b]  
- To begin your Grandeur adventure, you must first have completed the primary quest "[b]A Writ of Passage[/b]."  
- Once this is done, visit Ogden at the Counsel Building in The Belfry to pick up "[b]A Grand Plan[/b]" and help bring some holiday cheer to Bumble, who is feeling homesick.  
- Earn rewards to progress the new Grandeur Event Curio!  

[b]Aurora Ridge - New Limited-Time Venture[/b]  
- Families are looking forward to lighting the Grandeur bonfire but need to ensure it’s safe to gather.  
- The [b]A Grand Plan[/b] quest must be completed before playing the Venture.  
- New Grandeur-themed encounters can be found throughout the game, featuring enemies like Mistle Bundle Snow Howlers and Bell-Slinging Gobos.  
- Assist travelers trying to bring presents to the Belfry and more!  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/6c94f647c393e53622a8c0bbd8b60d4eec04186c.png[/img]

[h2]Combat[/h2]
Over the last few months, combat has steadily sharpened with each new update—attacks are snappier, evades flow smoother, and Classes have gained a few slick moves. In this update, we’re thrilled to introduce universal Jump Cancels, no longer limited to specific attacks! This long-awaited change clears old hurdles and opens a whole new realm of combos and strategies. While we’ll keep tweaking it over time, Jump Cancels are already in a great place. So dive in, leap into action, and enjoy the newfound freedom as you carve your path to victory!

[h3]General[/h3]

[b]Jump Cancels[/b]  
- Universally enabled Jump Cancels for all Classes from most attacks. This works similarly to the rules for Evade Cancels. If you are able to Evade Cancel an attack, then you should be able to Jump Cancel it.  
- It is now possible to Jump Cancel in any direction. For moves that had the old version of Jump Cancels, you were actually limited to jumping in a very specific way. This is no longer a limitation and should make Jump Cancels feel more intuitive.  

[b]Jump[/b]  
- Jump now carries your momentum in ways that feel more natural than before. You may notice that your jumps will go a bit further now when moving quickly.  

[b]Bees[/b]  
- Aces are now properly cleansed of Bees when using a Healing Shrine.  

[h3]Classes[/h3]

[b]Sentinel[/b]  
- Fixed an issue that caused Steady Strikes to not Block Break enemies as expected. This should now work consistently for all hits.  
- Fixed an issue that caused Evade/Dash Attacks to not trigger properly with Goji’s Echo equipped.  

[b]Pyroclast[/b]  
- Fixed an issue that caused Blazing Roar to not Block Break enemies as expected. This should now work consistently for all hits.  
- Fixed an issue that caused Evade/Dash Attacks to not trigger properly with Goji’s Echo equipped.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/bc9a8a7e970361f614949f14bbbc2b635913e921.png[/img]

[b]Rockbreaker[/b]  
- [b]Powderkeg Punch:[/b] Performing Combo Finishers increases the charge speed of Powderkeg Punch by about 20%. This buff lasts for 25 seconds and stacks with each Combo Finisher performed.  
- Improved visuals of Skyward Swing vortex.  
- Allowing players to rotate near the end of Skyward Swing.  
- Fixed an issue that caused Evade/Dash Attacks to not trigger properly with Goji’s Echo equipped.  

[b]Shadowstriker[/b]  
- Fixed an issue that caused Lightning Step and Silver Strikes to not Block Break enemies as expected. This should now work consistently for all hits.  
- Fixed an issue that caused the Class Mechanic to whiff against grounded enemies.  
- Fixed an issue that caused Shooting Stars to not hit grounded enemies properly.  
- Fixed an issue that caused Evade/Dash Attacks to not trigger properly with Goji’s Echo equipped.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/326f6b9bbb36fcfcac155e31c9fdf19a59769a10.png[/img]

[h3]Enemies[/h3]
For this update, the changes to enemies really revolve around quality-of-life improvements for the player. The most significant change centers around Pangojira, which will increase the challenge of this Boss in some pretty significant ways. Let us know how it feels!

[b]Pangor[/b]  
- Fixed an issue that caused Aces to go through Pangors during their Vulnerable state.  

[b]Quivertail[/b]  
- Fixed an issue where the wakeup attack had a Red VFX instead of Yellow VFX.  

[b]Boarealis Stoutswine[/b]  
- Allowing Boar charge to hit enemies and friends.  

[b]Gobo Brute[/b]  
- Allowing Brute charge to hit enemies and friends.  

[b]Training Room Dummy[/b]  
- Fixed an issue where players weren’t able to jump over the Enraged training room dummy.  

[b]Snow Howler[/b]  
- Lowered Defense to be more in line with Gobos (from 1.0 to 0.75).  

[b]Yxil[/b]  
- Adjusted the size of ground projectiles so that it’s more reflective of the visual.  

[b]Pangojira[/b]  
- Fixed an issue that caused Pangojira to not perform the forward Rockwave attack.  
- Takes more hits to kill Elite Pangors in the boss fight.  
- Elites spawn quicker.  

[b]The Shepherd[/b]  
- Fixed an issue that allowed the Shepherd to get interrupted and launched.  
- Removed homing from Shepherd’s projectile.  

[b]The Seamstress[/b]  
- Improved the visual of the tornado so that it matches the color scheme of the enemy.  
- Fixed an issue that allowed the Seamstress to get interrupted and launched.  
  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/8736661e397ffc735e742b78049f8ef521c07b0a.png[/img]

[h2]UI/UX[/h2]
We’ve polished your interface and navigation so you can focus on the action, not the menus. Quick-hitting prompts, intuitive layouts, and subtle improvements throughout mean more time battling baddies and enjoying your winter wonderland—no compass required.

[h3]Missions and Map[/h3]
- Improved Umbra Mission panel display.  
- Improved matchmaking messaging into the world map.  
- Added a button on the map to return to the Belfry.  
- Fixed recommended gear score not showing as red when players don’t have a high enough gear score when entering a mission.  
- Added a prompt for the winter event interactable on the Belfry.  

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]

- Improved layout of player HUD blades.

notes.title: The Future of Matchmaking in Towerborne
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44237228/894e4db462ff05922991386ac1c8936120666ea0.png[/img]
Hello Aces!

I wanted to give you an update on where we are with Matchmaking after the release of the first iteration of Group Finder. This letter will talk about 3 things:[list]
[*]The Current State of the Group Finder
[*]Group Finder Next Steps
[*]Turning Off the Previous Matchmaking System
[/list]
[h2]The Current State of the Group Finder[/h2]

As you know, in my first Letter to the Community, we talked about how we were not happy with the matchmaking solution that had initially shipped with Towerborne. So much so that we opted to turn off Discovery Mission matchmaking and work on building a true Group Finder.

The first iteration of the Group Finder has been out for several days now and it makes some fundamental changes to how you find a party. This iteration is quite basic: You select the type of group you’re looking for and the Danger Level ranges you’re comfortable playing in. After that, we match you into any open groups that meet your criteria.

[h2]Group Finder Next Steps[/h2]

These changes are merely a stop-gap while we continue the work on the larger changes; changes that will put more control into your hands.

Over the coming months we will be focused on improving the experience of finding, and playing with, a group. Some of the future changes to Group Finder include:

[list]
[*]Use Group Finder on the Map or on the Belfry, and be able to move between the two spaces without canceling or resetting the Finder.
[*]Show a list of Parties with an opening and filter according to your preferences.
[*]No more “blind” searching and hoping you get added.
[*]Change/Edit the Group Finder “rules” at any point while searching for players.
[/list]
These are just some of the improvements that we have in store, with others in discussion as you read this.

Now, I wasn’t born yesterday (in fact, it was the day BEFORE yesterday), so I know one of the unspoken questions you might have: “What about join-in-progress?”

Well, that one is a bit tricksy.

You see, join-in-progress is a lot more complicated than you might imagine and it will take no small amount of effort to implement if we decide to pursue this. Rest assured, we are going to be looking at this functionality and what it will take to support it. That said, don’t expect it anytime soon, or even SOON™.

[h2]A Quick Note About Finding a Group[/h2]

Right now you can’t see how many players are searching for a group—we know this is an issue, but we wanted to get this out so we can continue to improve it over time. This will be fixed in a later iteration (as noted above), but in the meantime, we highly recommend that you SEARCH for a group first before you start a group.

[h2]Turning Off the Previous Matchmaking System[/h2]

Now that we’ve released the Group Finder we are going to turn off the on-tile Matchmaking system on Ventures and on the special group tiles we released last month. This should encourage everyone to move to using the Group Finder and reduce the number of spaces where players are looking for a Party and help us focus our efforts into improving the new system.

[i]Expect this to happen in the coming days.[/i]

[h2]Closing Thoughts[/h2]

Finally, thank you SO, so much for your patience and continued support of Towerborne. We cannot thank you enough and it’s amazing to see all your thoughts and feedback. Rest assured, we are working to continue to improve the game, and we absolutely cannot wait for you to see what else we have in store for you.

Please, continue to give us feedback and we will continue to improve this system AND the game!

From the bottom of our Gauntlets: Thank you!

-Not Really a Jedi

[h2]Gameplay & Exploration[/h2]
[list]

[list]
[*][b]No More Overly Stubborn Foes:[/b] Fixed an issue that caused Yxil and Pangojira to stop taking damage when reaching specific health thresholds. Damage now occurs as expected when hitting these enemies.
